paragraphs.title: The Beginning of the Wall and the Northern Gates

easy.explanation: Eliashib and the priests built the sheep gate.
easy.q: Which gate did Eliashib the high priest and the priests build?

easy.explanation: The men of Jericho built next unto Eliashib.
The sons of Hassenaah built the fish gate.
easy.q: Which gate did the sons of Hassenaah build?

answers: They sanctified it and set up its doors
They changed it into the dung gate
medium.explanation: They sanctified the gate and set up its doors.
medium.q: What did the priests do after building the sheep gate?

medium.explanation: The verses describe several groups building next to one another.
medium.q: What does the work of the men of Jericho and Zaccur show?

answers: They did not take part in the work
medium.explanation: The phrase describes the nobles of Tekoa refusing to work.
medium.q: What does the phrase “put not their necks to the work” mean?

answers: They set up the doors, locks, and bars
They worked only beside their homes
challenge.explanation: They laid the beams and set up the doors, locks, and bars of the fish gate.
challenge.q: What detail distinguishes the sons of Hassenaah from the workers around them?

answers: The old gate, the sheep gate, the fish gate
The sheep gate, the fish gate, the old gate
The fish gate, the sheep gate, the dung gate
challenge.explanation: The sheep gate appears first, followed by the fish gate and then the old gate.
challenge.q: What is the correct order of the gates mentioned at the beginning of the passage?

answers: The nobles of Tekoa refused to work
challenge.explanation: The passage says that the Tekoites repaired, but their nobles did not work.
challenge.q: What appears alongside the cooperation at the beginning of the work?

paragraphs.title: Participation by Local Communities and Officials

answers: The men of Gibeon and Mizpah
easy.explanation: The men of Gibeon and Mizpah are named among those who repaired the wall.
easy.q: Which local people are named as taking part in the building?

easy.explanation: Jedaiah repaired over against his house.
easy.q: Who repaired over against his house?

easy.explanation: Shallum repaired the wall, he and his daughters.

medium.explanation: Uzziel was a goldsmith, and Hananiah was the son of one of the apothecaries; both repaired the wall.
medium.q: What does the passage show about the participation of craftsmen?

answers: Rulers of districts are named as responsible for sections
They built every gate by themselves
medium.explanation: Several rulers of districts are mentioned as repairing portions of the wall.
medium.q: Why can some officials be viewed as leaders of the work?

answers: Took responsibility for a section of work
medium.explanation: The word describes taking responsibility for building or repairing a section.
medium.q: What does “repaired” mean in the context of this passage?

answers: Many worked opposite or near their homes
The work was done only at the gates
challenge.explanation: Jedaiah and others are specifically described as working opposite their houses.
challenge.q: What connection between homes and the work appears repeatedly in the passage?

answers: The effort included people from the surrounding area
The building was limited to individual families
challenge.explanation: The passage names people from Gibeon and Mizpah, not only residents of Jerusalem.
challenge.q: What does the participation of people from Gibeon and Mizpah show about the scope of the effort?

answers: From the sheep gate to the fish gate
From the valley gate to the dung gate
From the water gate to the horse gate
challenge.explanation: They repaired the valley gate and a thousand cubits of the wall unto the dung gate.
challenge.q: Which relatively long section was assigned to Hanun and the inhabitants of Zanoah?

paragraphs.title: The Work Continues by Districts, Families, and Homes

easy.explanation: After Nehemiah, the Levites repaired the wall.
easy.q: Who repaired after Nehemiah the son of Azbuk?

easy.explanation: Benjamin and Hashub repaired over against their house.
easy.q: Who repaired over against their house?

easy.explanation: The goldsmiths and merchants repaired between the corner and the sheep gate.
easy.q: Which craftsmen are mentioned near the end of the passage?

answers: An additional section of the wall
A measurement for a new gate
medium.explanation: The phrase indicates that a person or group took responsibility for an additional section.
medium.q: What does “another piece” mean in this chapter?

answers: By districts, families, homes, and occupations
Without any division among the workers
medium.explanation: The passage mentions district rulers, families, homes, Levites, priests, and craftsmen.
medium.q: How is the work divided in this passage?

answers: They worked alongside the other groups
medium.explanation: Both Levites and priests are named as repairing sections of the wall.
medium.q: Why are the Levites and priests notable in the list of builders?

answers: The work involved direct local responsibility
They did not know the area
They worked only at the gates
challenge.explanation: Working opposite one's home connects the worker directly with the section being repaired.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the fact that many people worked opposite their homes?

answers: Levites, priests, families, Nethinims, and craftsmen
Priests, men of Jericho, Sanballat, and Tobiah
challenge.explanation: These groups are all mentioned in the order and progress of the work.
challenge.q: Which general sequence of groups appears from the middle to the end of the passage?

answers: The Nethinims dwelt in Ophel and repaired by the water gate
All the work was done at the sheep gate
challenge.explanation: The Nethinims are said to dwell in Ophel and repair opposite the water gate.
challenge.q: Which easily overlooked detail is stated in the passage?

paragraphs.title: Enemy Mockery, Nehemiah’s Prayer, and Half the Wall Completed

easy.explanation: Sanballat was angry and mocked the Jews.
easy.q: Who mocked the Jews when he heard that they were building the wall?

easy.explanation: Tobiah the Ammonite was with Sanballat and added to the mockery.

answers: To one third of its height
easy.explanation: The wall was joined together unto the half thereof.
easy.q: How far was the wall joined by the end of the passage?

medium.explanation: Nehemiah prayed that the reproach would return upon the mockers.
medium.q: How did Nehemiah respond to the mockery of the enemies?

answers: The Jews’ ability to build a strong wall
The number of gates in the city
The priests’ duties in the temple
medium.explanation: Their words mocked whether the Jews could finish and strengthen the wall.
medium.q: What did Sanballat and Tobiah attempt to cast doubt upon?

answers: The wall was joined to half its height, and the people had a mind to work
medium.explanation: The wall was joined, and the people continued with determination.
medium.q: What was the result of the work despite the mockery?

answers: Enemy mockery versus the people’s determination
Peace in the city versus halted work
The priests’ refusal versus the Nethinims’ departure
challenge.explanation: The enemies mocked, but the people continued and had a mind to work.
challenge.q: What major contrast appears at the end of the passage?

answers: That the reproach return upon their own head
That they receive the city gates
challenge.explanation: Nehemiah asked God to turn their reproach back upon their own head.
challenge.q: What did Nehemiah ask concerning the reproach of the enemies?

answers: It shows real progress, but not complete completion
It shows that the work had not begun
It shows that half the wall had been destroyed
challenge.explanation: The wall had made substantial progress, but the work was not yet finished.
challenge.q: Why is the phrase “unto the half thereof” significant?
